Marissa / Mina / Jane — technical appendix below. I'll attach the high-level dataflow diagram (redwood-dataflow-diagram.png) and we can convert to a one-page appendix.

Technical appendix (summary):
- Scope of "customer text": request/response payloads submitted via API/SDK, file uploads to customer-managed storage connectors, and structured fields submitted as part of calls. Telemetry (client SDK metrics) is out-of-scope for this attestation unless explicitly listed.

- Training usage: Redwood does not use customer text to train or fine-tune production or internal models in hosted or dedicated environments. Private (customer-managed on-prem/VPC) deployments are under customer control; Redwood will not access or use data for training unless explicitly contracted and documented.

- Ephemeral request logs: default retention 7 days for request logs kept for routing/SLAs and debugging (configurable per-customer). Logs older than TTL are deleted by automated jobs; deletion is implemented as a two-stage tombstone then purge to allow safe replication. Typical tombstone delay: 24 hours; purge job runs within 48 hours after tombstone (so max visible deletion window ~72 hours).

- KV / prefix caching: KV cache is in-memory on serving hosts with optional short-lived local persistence for cold-start; default TTL 6 hours for cache entries. Cache entries are not materialized to long-term storage.

- Snapshots & backups: model state snapshots and telemetry snapshots are taken per-cluster for operational recovery. Customer data snapshots (for Dedicated) are encrypted at-rest and retained for 30 days by default; longer retention is possible by contract. Cross-region backups are disabled by default for accounts that require US-only residency; if enabled, it's an opt-in and will be indicated explicitly.

- Archived logs and audit artifacts: retained for 90 days by default and available on request for compliance investigations; retention configurable.

- Evidence of purge: we can provide (a) purge job run logs with timestamps, (b) snapshot manifests showing deletion markers, and (c) KMS key rotation/deletion events showing ciphertext inaccessibility. For legal/forensics-grade evidence, we propose a signed purge report including job IDs, affected keys/object paths, and timestamps.

- Edge cases / exceptions: backups in long-term cold storage (e.g., for customers who request extended backups) may have longer retention; any such exceptions will be listed in the contract appendix. Debugging snapshots taken for incident investigation are time-limited and flagged; access is auditable and can be scoped to named personnel.

Next steps:
1) Mina: please review for legal language that should appear in the attestation (e.g., carve-outs, effective date, contact for notices).
2) Marissa: I'll produce the one-page appendix and include the diagram; can finalize by EOD Thu to meet the customer's timeline.
